title: Letters and Orchard
premise: Jude Reyes, a marine biologist who fled to a remote sea-turtle station after a devastating breakup, believes love is a debt he can no longer afford. When a freak snowstorm strands him with two estranged former lovers — brilliant conservation lawyer Mara Voss and charming documentary filmmaker Theo Lindqvist, the 'best mistake' of his twenties — old wounds and old desires resurface. As a land dispute threatens the station and Mara's case could either save it or destroy Jude's life's work, Jude must choose between the career that rebuilt him and the person who finally sees him whole. In the end, Jude realizes the choice was never between love and duty, but between hiding and living; he stays at the station, but no longer alone, as Mara chooses him over the partnership that defined her.
about_author: Bram Eriksen is the pen name of a former field researcher who spent six seasons counting nests on remote coastlines before turning to fiction. They write love stories for people who believe tenderness is a survival skill.

chapters.title: Counting Instead of Feeling
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On a cold October morning, Jude records the season's final turtle nest, narrating his life in data points to avoid feeling anything. A letter from the land trust arrives: the station's lease is under legal challenge. Emotional beat: guarded routine cracked by the first threat to his sanctuary.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Packing for a supplies run to the mainland, Jude finds an unsent letter to Theo from eight years ago and burns it in the woodstove. His colleague Priya teases him about a heart 'in the past tense.' Emotional beat: grief dressed up as tidiness.

chapters.title: Two Strangers at the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara arrives on the island to represent the trust's challenger — a resort developer — and is shocked to learn the station's lead biologist is Jude Reyes. She hasn't seen him since law school. Emotional beat: ambition colliding with dread.

chapters.title: The Storm That Changed the Map
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo lands on the island to film a puffin documentary just as the last ferry is canceled. At the dock he recognizes Mara — his ex — and then, at the station door, Jude. Emotional beat: the past arriving all at once, snow closing every exit.

chapters.title: Three Plates, One Table
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Stranded together, the three share an awkward first dinner. Old jokes resurface; so do old knives. Priya evacuates on the last supply flight, leaving Jude alone with his history. Emotional beat: comedy stretched over an open wound.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A storm surge strands a cold-stunned turtle on the beach; the three work through the night to rescue it. In the tank's green glow, Mara watches Jude's hands and remembers why she loved him. Emotional beat: shared purpose softening armor.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Snowbound with nothing but wine and a broken furnace, Theo confesses why he vanished from both their lives: a career built on leaving before being left. Jude throws him out into the snow. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude walks the storm-blinded beach to cool his rage and nearly walks into the surf; Mara finds him and pulls him back. Shaking, he admits he's been 'counting turtles instead of heartbreaks' for eight years. Emotional beat: the first honest crack.

chapters.title: Mara's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone with the case files, Mara realizes winning for the developer means destroying the station — and Jude. She drafts a strategy to flip the case and tells no one. Emotional beat: duty beginning to cost more than it pays.

chapters.title: Thaw Lines
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The storm breaks. Theo repairs the station fence as unspoken apology; Jude lets him, wordlessly. They fall into old rhythms — laughter first, then a kiss neither planned. Emotional beat: desire returning like a tide that never learned.

chapters.title: The Case Against the Station
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara's firm sends a replacement lawyer, signaling she's off the case; her partnership hangs on the developer's win. She hides the eviction timeline from Jude. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Nest Census
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude takes Mara on his nest survey; she asks real questions about the turtles and, dangerously, about him. He almost tells her about the letter he once wrote. Emotional beat: intimacy as risk assessment gone wrong.

chapters.title: Rival Tides
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers Mara's eviction timeline in her bag and, jealous and hurt, tells Jude — framing it as betrayal rather than strategy. Jude confronts Mara; she leaves for the mainland on the first ferry out. Emotional beat: love weaponized into rivalry.

chapters.title: The Empty Tank
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With Mara gone, the rescued turtle is released, and Jude watches it swim into grey water feeling nothing like triumph. He rereads Theo's old confession and his own burned letter's surviving draft. Emotional beat: hollow victory, honest inventory.

chapters.title: What Theo Filmed
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reviewing footage, Theo finds he's accidentally documented the station's ecological value — and Jude's quiet heroism. He realizes he can spend his career's capital to save the station, or keep himself safe. Emotional beat: a coward choosing courage.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the land trust hearing, Mara defects from her firm, presenting the station's case with Theo's footage as evidence. She wins the injunction but loses her partnership. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty folding.

chapters.title: The Person Who Sees Clearly
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude learns what Mara sacrificed and drives through the night to find her. He confesses the eight-year-old letter, the fear, the counting. She says she didn't need the letter — she needed him present. Emotional beat: the choice made aloud.

chapters.title: Terms of Return
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo returns to the station to say goodbye properly; Jude and Mara offer him friendship without history's weight. He accepts, filming one last scene — the three of them, unposed. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a new shape of love.

chapters.title: Season's First Nest
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Spring arrives; the station's lease is secured. Mara takes a conservation-law post on the mainland and commutes by ferry; Jude lets someone plan around him instead of around her leaving. Emotional beat: trust as daily practice.

chapters.title: The Letter, Finally Sent
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Jude gives Mara the reconstructed letter — not as confession but as gift. She reads it on the ferry and cries in front of strangers, unashamed. Emotional beat: the past tense becoming present.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's documentary premieres; the final shot is the released turtle's wake, and the credits name the station. Watching from the back row, Theo feels grief and gratitude coexist. Emotional beat: the rival becoming witness.

chapters.title: Orchard at the Station's Edge
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude and Mara plant an apple orchard beside the station — something slow, seasonal, that requires staying. The first turtle hatchlings race for the sea as they watch, hand in hand. Emotional beat: love as a thing planted, not survived.
